findings.what_changed: No consolidated results have ever been filed. Every one of this issuer's 25 machine-readable filings, from 2018 to 2025, is standalone.
findings.why_it_matters: Standalone accounts describe the listed entity alone. Where a lender sits inside a group, they need not describe the business that carries the risk: SREI Infrastructure's standalone accounts reported zero advances because the loan book sat in a subsidiary. Without a consolidated basis, group leverage cannot be read from this source at all. This issuer is part of the Reliance Capital group.
findings.investigate: Establish whether the issuer has subsidiaries at all. If it does, obtain the group's consolidated annual report; if it is itself a subsidiary, read the parent alongside it.
findings.counterevidence: A standalone-only filer may simply have no subsidiaries, in which case standalone IS the group and nothing is missing.

findings.what_changed: Profit after tax for the quarter ending 2020-03-31 (Consolidated) was a loss of Rs 69 crore, against a trailing four-quarter median profit of Rs 101 crore.
findings.why_it_matters: A swing into loss consumes the equity buffer directly and is the point at which rating agencies and lenders typically reassess. For a lender it usually means provisions were raised rather than that income fell.
findings.investigate: Establish whether the loss is provisioning or write-off, and whether it was pre-announced. Compare with lenders of the same type in the same quarter: a sector-wide provisioning change is not issuer-specific news.
findings.counterevidence: A one-time provision, an accounting transition, or a regulator-mandated change in provisioning norms can each produce a single loss-making quarter.

findings.what_changed: Impairment on financial instruments for the quarter ending 2020-12-31 (Consolidated) was Rs 2,833 crore against Rs 26 crore in the same quarter a year earlier (+10716%).
findings.why_it_matters: Impairment is the issuer's own admission that the loan book is worth less than previously carried. Compared year on year rather than against the trailing quarter, it is not confounded by the seasonality of NBFC provisioning.
findings.investigate: Determine which book the impairment sits in and whether stage-2 and stage-3 balances moved with it. Check whether the issuer changed its ECL assumptions in the same filing.
findings.counterevidence: Loan-book growth raises impairment proportionally; scale the move against the change in advances before treating it as deterioration.

findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: 50 of 57 payment-related attachments (87%) are scanned images with no text layer and could not be read.

findings.investigate: Open a sample directly. If the issuer's filings are routinely scanned, this channel needs optical character recognition before it can be relied on for this name.

findings.what_changed: The 45-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2020-09-30 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 62 days. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.

findings.what_changed: Profit after tax for the quarter ending 2020-06-30 (Consolidated) was a loss of Rs 1,095 crore, against a trailing four-quarter median profit of Rs 50 crore.
findings.why_it_matters: A swing into loss consumes the equity buffer directly and is the point at which rating agencies and lenders typically reassess. For a lender it usually means provisions were raised rather than that income fell.
findings.investigate: Establish whether the loss is provisioning or write-off, and whether it was pre-announced. Compare with lenders of the same type in the same quarter: a sector-wide provisioning change is not issuer-specific news.
findings.counterevidence: A one-time provision, an accounting transition, or a regulator-mandated change in provisioning norms can each produce a single loss-making quarter.

findings.what_changed: Profit after tax for the quarter ending 2023-09-30 (Consolidated) was a loss of Rs 239 crore, against a trailing four-quarter median profit of Rs 325 crore.
findings.why_it_matters: A swing into loss consumes the equity buffer directly and is the point at which rating agencies and lenders typically reassess. For a lender it usually means provisions were raised rather than that income fell.
findings.investigate: Establish whether the loss is provisioning or write-off, and whether it was pre-announced. Compare with lenders of the same type in the same quarter: a sector-wide provisioning change is not issuer-specific news.
findings.counterevidence: A one-time provision, an accounting transition, or a regulator-mandated change in provisioning norms can each produce a single loss-making quarter.

findings.why_it_matters: Equity over assets is the buffer between losses and creditors. In the testing behind this tool it separated failed from surviving lenders better than a weighted multi-factor index did, which is why it is reported on its own rather than folded into a score.

findings.why_it_matters: The exchange's own structured data is internally inconsistent here. Any ratio or trend computed across this filing and its neighbours would be wrong by orders of magnitude, so the figures are excluded from every numeric test rather than rescaled by a guessed factor.

findings.what_changed: Credit Rating: Indiabulls Housing Finance Limited has informed the Exchange regarding Credit RatingThis is with reference to the communication Indiabulls Housing Finance Limited [IBH] received from the rating agency CRISIL on October 16, 2019. The rating committee of CRISIL
findings.why_it_matters: A rating action is a third party revising its view. Downgrades frequently cluster before a payment failure, and the commentary usually names the concern.
findings.investigate: Open the attachment and record what specifically was said, by whom, and whether the issuer's next filing addressed it.

findings.what_changed: Impairment on financial instruments for the quarter ending 2022-12-31 (Consolidated) was Rs 267 crore against Rs 53 crore in the same quarter a year earlier (+399%).
findings.why_it_matters: Impairment is the issuer's own admission that the loan book is worth less than previously carried. Compared year on year rather than against the trailing quarter, it is not confounded by the seasonality of NBFC provisioning.
findings.investigate: Determine which book the impairment sits in and whether stage-2 and stage-3 balances moved with it. Check whether the issuer changed its ECL assumptions in the same filing.
findings.counterevidence: Loan-book growth raises impairment proportionally; scale the move against the change in advances before treating it as deterioration.

findings.what_changed: Profit after tax for the quarter ending 2024-09-30 (Consolidated) was a loss of Rs 2,761 crore, against a trailing four-quarter median profit of Rs 311 crore.
findings.why_it_matters: A swing into loss consumes the equity buffer directly and is the point at which rating agencies and lenders typically reassess. For a lender it usually means provisions were raised rather than that income fell.
findings.investigate: Establish whether the loss is provisioning or write-off, and whether it was pre-announced. Compare with lenders of the same type in the same quarter: a sector-wide provisioning change is not issuer-specific news.
findings.counterevidence: A one-time provision, an accounting transition, or a regulator-mandated change in provisioning norms can each produce a single loss-making quarter.

findings.what_changed: 4 of 26 quarters between 2018-09-30 and 2024-12-31 have no machine-readable filing: 2019-03-31, 2019-06-30, 2019-09-30, 2019-12-31.
findings.why_it_matters: A gap is not evidence of a problem, but it bounds what can be claimed. Any trend drawn across a gap is an assumption.
findings.investigate: NSE published results XBRL only from about 2019. For earlier periods use the results PDF attached to the announcement stream.

findings.what_changed: The most recent parseable results filing was disseminated 2025-02-12, 608 days ago.
findings.why_it_matters: An issuer that has stopped filing cannot be assessed. For a delisted or suspended issuer this is expected; for an active one it is itself the finding.
findings.investigate: Confirm whether the issuer is still listed and still required to file.
findings.counterevidence: Delisting, suspension, merger or voluntary wind-down all stop the filing stream legitimately.

findings.what_changed: The 77-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2020-06-30 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 32 days. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-09-15 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Total income for 2024-04-01 to 2024-12-31 was filed as Rs 5,766 crore, but the 3 quarters inside that period, as originally filed, sum to Rs 5,907 crore - a difference of Rs -141 crore (-2.4%).
findings.why_it_matters: A cumulative figure that does not equal the sum of its parts means one of the quarters was restated after it was first reported, or an item was reclassified between periods. Either way, the originally published quarter is no longer what the issuer stands behind.

issuers.name: PNB Housing Finance
issuers.outcome: Severe funding stress and a contested capital raise; survived

findings.what_changed: The 45-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2018-09-30 passed with no filing. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2018-11-14 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Credit Rating: PNB Housing Finance Limited has informed the Exchange regarding Credit Rating Downgrade by India Rating of its NCD Programme of INR 280 billion from INDAAA/RWN to INDAA+/Stable
findings.why_it_matters: A rating action is a third party revising its view. Downgrades frequently cluster before a payment failure, and the commentary usually names the concern.
findings.investigate: Open the attachment and record what specifically was said, by whom, and whether the issuer's next filing addressed it.

findings.what_changed: 4 of 26 quarters between 2018-09-30 and 2024-12-31 have no machine-readable filing: 2019-03-31, 2019-06-30, 2019-09-30, 2022-06-30.
findings.why_it_matters: A gap is not evidence of a problem, but it bounds what can be claimed. Any trend drawn across a gap is an assumption.
findings.investigate: NSE published results XBRL only from about 2019. For earlier periods use the results PDF attached to the announcement stream.

findings.what_changed: The most recent parseable results filing was disseminated 2025-01-22, 629 days ago.
findings.why_it_matters: An issuer that has stopped filing cannot be assessed. For a delisted or suspended issuer this is expected; for an active one it is itself the finding.
findings.investigate: Confirm whether the issuer is still listed and still required to file.
findings.counterevidence: Delisting, suspension, merger or voluntary wind-down all stop the filing stream legitimately.

findings.what_changed: The 45-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2019-12-31 passed with no filing. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-02-14 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Impairment on financial instruments for the quarter ending 2022-12-31 was Rs 255 crore against Rs 129 crore in the same quarter a year earlier (+97%). The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: Impairment is the issuer's own admission that the loan book is worth less than previously carried. Compared year on year rather than against the trailing quarter, it is not confounded by the seasonality of NBFC provisioning.
findings.investigate: Determine which book the impairment sits in and whether stage-2 and stage-3 balances moved with it. Check whether the issuer changed its ECL assumptions in the same filing.
findings.counterevidence: Loan-book growth raises impairment proportionally; scale the move against the change in advances before treating it as deterioration.

findings.what_changed: The 45-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2019-12-31 passed with no filing. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-02-14 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Impairment on financial instruments for the quarter ending 2024-03-31 (Consolidated) was Rs 236 crore against Rs 10 crore in the same quarter a year earlier (+2342%).
findings.why_it_matters: Impairment is the issuer's own admission that the loan book is worth less than previously carried. Compared year on year rather than against the trailing quarter, it is not confounded by the seasonality of NBFC provisioning.
findings.investigate: Determine which book the impairment sits in and whether stage-2 and stage-3 balances moved with it. Check whether the issuer changed its ECL assumptions in the same filing.
findings.counterevidence: Loan-book growth raises impairment proportionally; scale the move against the change in advances before treating it as deterioration.

findings.what_changed: Profit after tax for the quarter ending 2024-06-30 (Standalone) was a loss of Rs 23 crore, against a trailing four-quarter median profit of Rs 144 crore.
findings.why_it_matters: A swing into loss consumes the equity buffer directly and is the point at which rating agencies and lenders typically reassess. For a lender it usually means provisions were raised rather than that income fell.
findings.investigate: Establish whether the loss is provisioning or write-off, and whether it was pre-announced. Compare with lenders of the same type in the same quarter: a sector-wide provisioning change is not issuer-specific news.
findings.counterevidence: A one-time provision, an accounting transition, or a regulator-mandated change in provisioning norms can each produce a single loss-making quarter.

findings.what_changed: The 45-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2018-06-30 passed with no filing. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2018-08-14 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Profit after tax for the quarter ending 2019-12-31 (Standalone) was a loss of Rs 13 crore, against a trailing four-quarter median profit of Rs 22 crore.
findings.why_it_matters: A swing into loss consumes the equity buffer directly and is the point at which rating agencies and lenders typically reassess. For a lender it usually means provisions were raised rather than that income fell.
findings.investigate: Establish whether the loss is provisioning or write-off, and whether it was pre-announced. Compare with lenders of the same type in the same quarter: a sector-wide provisioning change is not issuer-specific news.
findings.counterevidence: A one-time provision, an accounting transition, or a regulator-mandated change in provisioning norms can each produce a single loss-making quarter.

findings.what_changed: Total income for 2020-04-01 to 2021-03-31 was filed as Rs 1,722 crore, but the 4 quarters inside that period, as originally filed, sum to Rs 1,889 crore - a difference of Rs -167 crore (-9.7%).
findings.why_it_matters: A cumulative figure that does not equal the sum of its parts means one of the quarters was restated after it was first reported, or an item was reclassified between periods. Either way, the originally published quarter is no longer what the issuer stands behind.

findings.investigate: Compare the two filings directly and find the restated line. Ask whether the restatement was disclosed as such, and whether it changed any covenant or ratio the issuer reports.
findings.counterevidence: Ind AS transition, a discontinued operation, a business combination, or a merger accounted for retrospectively can all legitimately change comparatives - but each should be explicitly disclosed in the filing.

findings.what_changed: Impairment on financial instruments for the quarter ending 2021-03-31 (Standalone) was Rs 149 crore against Rs 1 crore in the same quarter a year earlier (+17602%).
findings.why_it_matters: Impairment is the issuer's own admission that the loan book is worth less than previously carried. Compared year on year rather than against the trailing quarter, it is not confounded by the seasonality of NBFC provisioning.
findings.investigate: Determine which book the impairment sits in and whether stage-2 and stage-3 balances moved with it. Check whether the issuer changed its ECL assumptions in the same filing.
findings.counterevidence: Loan-book growth raises impairment proportionally; scale the move against the change in advances before treating it as deterioration.

findings.what_changed: Equity as a share of total assets fell from 15.9% for the year ended 2014 to 10.4% for the year ended 2015 (-35% relative).
findings.why_it_matters: Equity over assets is the buffer between losses and creditors. In the testing behind this tool it separated failed from surviving lenders better than a weighted multi-factor index did, which is why it is reported on its own rather than folded into a score.

findings.investigate: Confirm the figure against the audited balance sheet, and establish whether the fall is losses, a write-down, or a distribution. Check whether regulatory capital ratios moved with it - they use a different numerator.
findings.counterevidence: A capital raise in the following year, a change in the reporting entity, or a one-off accounting adjustment can each move this ratio without the underlying buffer changing.

findings.what_changed: The 60-day SEBI LODR deadline for consolidated results for the period ending 2019-03-31 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 31 days.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2019-05-30 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Credit Rating: Bajaj Finance Limited has informed the Exchange about Credit Rating that S&P Global Ratings has, vide its letter dated 26 June 2020, downgraded the credit rating of the Company from Long term rating of BBB-/Negative and Short-term rating of A-3 to Long term ra
findings.why_it_matters: A rating action is a third party revising its view. Downgrades frequently cluster before a payment failure, and the commentary usually names the concern.
findings.investigate: Open the attachment and record what specifically was said, by whom, and whether the issuer's next filing addressed it.

findings.what_changed: The most recent parseable results filing was disseminated 2025-01-29, 622 days ago.
findings.why_it_matters: An issuer that has stopped filing cannot be assessed. For a delisted or suspended issuer this is expected; for an active one it is itself the finding.
findings.investigate: Confirm whether the issuer is still listed and still required to file.
findings.counterevidence: Delisting, suspension, merger or voluntary wind-down all stop the filing stream legitimately.

findings.what_changed: 3 of 26 quarters between 2018-09-30 and 2024-12-31 have no machine-readable filing: 2019-03-31, 2019-06-30, 2019-09-30.
findings.why_it_matters: A gap is not evidence of a problem, but it bounds what can be claimed. Any trend drawn across a gap is an assumption.
findings.investigate: NSE published results XBRL only from about 2019. For earlier periods use the results PDF attached to the announcement stream.

findings.what_changed: The 77-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2020-06-30 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 30 days. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-09-15 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Impairment on financial instruments for the quarter ending 2021-03-31 was Rs 977 crore against Rs 27 crore in the same quarter a year earlier (+3486%). The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: Impairment is the issuer's own admission that the loan book is worth less than previously carried. Compared year on year rather than against the trailing quarter, it is not confounded by the seasonality of NBFC provisioning.
findings.investigate: Determine which book the impairment sits in and whether stage-2 and stage-3 balances moved with it. Check whether the issuer changed its ECL assumptions in the same filing.
findings.counterevidence: Loan-book growth raises impairment proportionally; scale the move against the change in advances before treating it as deterioration.

findings.what_changed: 32 of 32 payment-related attachments (100%) are scanned images with no text layer and could not be read.
findings.why_it_matters: A payment disclosure that cannot be read is not a disclosure that says nothing. Where most attachments are unreadable, the absence of a payment finding for this issuer carries no weight either way.
findings.investigate: Open a sample directly. If the issuer's filings are routinely scanned, this channel needs optical character recognition before it can be relied on for this name.

findings.what_changed: The most recent parseable results filing was disseminated 2025-01-31, 620 days ago.
findings.why_it_matters: An issuer that has stopped filing cannot be assessed. For a delisted or suspended issuer this is expected; for an active one it is itself the finding.
findings.investigate: Confirm whether the issuer is still listed and still required to file.
findings.counterevidence: Delisting, suspension, merger or voluntary wind-down all stop the filing stream legitimately.

findings.what_changed: The 45-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2020-09-30 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 58 days. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-11-14 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.why_it_matters: The exchange's own structured data is internally inconsistent here. Any ratio or trend computed across this filing and its neighbours would be wrong by orders of magnitude, so the figures are excluded from every numeric test rather than rescaled by a guessed factor.

findings.what_changed: The 77-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2020-06-30 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 36 days. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-09-15 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Impairment on financial instruments for the quarter ending 2020-12-31 was Rs 445 crore against Rs 136 crore in the same quarter a year earlier (+227%). The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: Impairment is the issuer's own admission that the loan book is worth less than previously carried. Compared year on year rather than against the trailing quarter, it is not confounded by the seasonality of NBFC provisioning.
findings.investigate: Determine which book the impairment sits in and whether stage-2 and stage-3 balances moved with it. Check whether the issuer changed its ECL assumptions in the same filing.
findings.counterevidence: Loan-book growth raises impairment proportionally; scale the move against the change in advances before treating it as deterioration.

findings.what_changed: The most recent parseable results filing was disseminated 2025-02-01, 619 days ago.
findings.why_it_matters: An issuer that has stopped filing cannot be assessed. For a delisted or suspended issuer this is expected; for an active one it is itself the finding.
findings.investigate: Confirm whether the issuer is still listed and still required to file.
findings.counterevidence: Delisting, suspension, merger or voluntary wind-down all stop the filing stream legitimately.

findings.what_changed: 2 of 26 quarters between 2018-09-30 and 2024-12-31 have no machine-readable filing: 2019-06-30, 2019-09-30.
findings.why_it_matters: A gap is not evidence of a problem, but it bounds what can be claimed. Any trend drawn across a gap is an assumption.
findings.investigate: NSE published results XBRL only from about 2019. For earlier periods use the results PDF attached to the announcement stream.

findings.what_changed: The 77-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2020-06-30 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 49 days. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-09-15 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Credit Rating: This is to inform you that Fitch Ratings has affirmed Muthoot Finance Limited's BB Long Term Issuer Default Ratings. Fitch Ratings has removed the Rating Watch Negative on the Issuer Default Rating and revised the Outlook to Stable . Enclosing herewith the Pre
findings.why_it_matters: A rating action is a third party revising its view. Downgrades frequently cluster before a payment failure, and the commentary usually names the concern.
findings.investigate: Open the attachment and record what specifically was said, by whom, and whether the issuer's next filing addressed it.

findings.what_changed: Impairment on financial instruments for the quarter ending 2024-09-30 (Consolidated) was Rs 420 crore against Rs 81 crore in the same quarter a year earlier (+417%).
findings.why_it_matters: Impairment is the issuer's own admission that the loan book is worth less than previously carried. Compared year on year rather than against the trailing quarter, it is not confounded by the seasonality of NBFC provisioning.
findings.investigate: Determine which book the impairment sits in and whether stage-2 and stage-3 balances moved with it. Check whether the issuer changed its ECL assumptions in the same filing.
findings.counterevidence: Loan-book growth raises impairment proportionally; scale the move against the change in advances before treating it as deterioration.

findings.what_changed: The most recent parseable results filing was disseminated 2025-02-13, 607 days ago.
findings.why_it_matters: An issuer that has stopped filing cannot be assessed. For a delisted or suspended issuer this is expected; for an active one it is itself the finding.
findings.investigate: Confirm whether the issuer is still listed and still required to file.
findings.counterevidence: Delisting, suspension, merger or voluntary wind-down all stop the filing stream legitimately.

findings.why_it_matters: A cumulative figure that does not equal the sum of its parts means one of the quarters was restated after it was first reported, or an item was reclassified between periods. Either way, the originally published quarter is no longer what the issuer stands behind.

evidence.source: NSE XBRL, arithmetic on filed figures

findings.counterevidence: Ind AS transition, a discontinued operation, a business combination, or a merger accounted for retrospectively can all legitimately change comparatives - but each should be explicitly disclosed in the filing.

findings.what_changed: The most recent parseable results filing was disseminated 2025-01-24, 627 days ago.
findings.why_it_matters: An issuer that has stopped filing cannot be assessed. For a delisted or suspended issuer this is expected; for an active one it is itself the finding.
findings.investigate: Confirm whether the issuer is still listed and still required to file.
findings.counterevidence: Delisting, suspension, merger or voluntary wind-down all stop the filing stream legitimately.

findings.what_changed: The 77-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2020-06-30 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 36 days. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-09-15 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: News Verification: CANFINHOME : The Exchange has sought clarification from Can Fin Homes Limited with respect to recent news item captioned SRCS say RBI may probe detection of fraud in 37 accounts. The response from the Company is awaited.
findings.why_it_matters: The exchange only seeks clarification when a news report is material enough to move the price. It is a timestamped record that something was alleged in public that the issuer had not disclosed.
findings.investigate: Open the attachment and record what specifically was said, by whom, and whether the issuer's next filing addressed it.

findings.what_changed: The most recent parseable results filing was disseminated 2025-01-18, 633 days ago.
findings.why_it_matters: An issuer that has stopped filing cannot be assessed. For a delisted or suspended issuer this is expected; for an active one it is itself the finding.
findings.investigate: Confirm whether the issuer is still listed and still required to file.
findings.counterevidence: Delisting, suspension, merger or voluntary wind-down all stop the filing stream legitimately.

findings.what_changed: No consolidated results have ever been filed. Every one of this issuer's 22 machine-readable filings, from 2020 to 2025, is standalone.
findings.why_it_matters: Standalone accounts describe the listed entity alone. Where a lender sits inside a group, they need not describe the business that carries the risk: SREI Infrastructure's standalone accounts reported zero advances because the loan book sat in a subsidiary. Without a consolidated basis, group leverage cannot be read from this source at all. This issuer is part of the Canara Bank group.
findings.investigate: Establish whether the issuer has subsidiaries at all. If it does, obtain the group's consolidated annual report; if it is itself a subsidiary, read the parent alongside it.
findings.counterevidence: A standalone-only filer may simply have no subsidiaries, in which case standalone IS the group and nothing is missing.

findings.what_changed: 2 of 21 quarters between 2019-12-31 and 2024-12-31 have no machine-readable filing: 2022-06-30, 2022-09-30.
findings.why_it_matters: A gap is not evidence of a problem, but it bounds what can be claimed. Any trend drawn across a gap is an assumption.
findings.investigate: NSE published results XBRL only from about 2019. For earlier periods use the results PDF attached to the announcement stream.

findings.what_changed: The 60-day SEBI LODR deadline for consolidated results for the period ending 2019-03-31 passed with no filing.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2019-05-30 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: Impairment on financial instruments for the quarter ending 2021-06-30 was Rs 78 crore against Rs 22 crore in the same quarter a year earlier (+254%). The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: Impairment is the issuer's own admission that the loan book is worth less than previously carried. Compared year on year rather than against the trailing quarter, it is not confounded by the seasonality of NBFC provisioning.
findings.investigate: Determine which book the impairment sits in and whether stage-2 and stage-3 balances moved with it. Check whether the issuer changed its ECL assumptions in the same filing.
findings.counterevidence: Loan-book growth raises impairment proportionally; scale the move against the change in advances before treating it as deterioration.

findings.what_changed: Profit after tax for 2022-04-01 to 2022-12-31 was filed as Rs 232 crore, but the 3 quarters inside that period, as originally filed, sum to Rs 226 crore - a difference of Rs 6 crore (+2.5%).
findings.why_it_matters: A cumulative figure that does not equal the sum of its parts means one of the quarters was restated after it was first reported, or an item was reclassified between periods. Either way, the originally published quarter is no longer what the issuer stands behind.

evidence.source: NSE XBRL, arithmetic on filed figures

findings.investigate: Compare the two filings directly and find the restated line. Ask whether the restatement was disclosed as such, and whether it changed any covenant or ratio the issuer reports.
findings.counterevidence: Ind AS transition, a discontinued operation, a business combination, or a merger accounted for retrospectively can all legitimately change comparatives - but each should be explicitly disclosed in the filing.

findings.what_changed: Credit Rating: Manappuram Finance Limited has informed the Exchange regarding Credit RatingPursuant to Regulation 30 and other applicable provisions of the Listing Regulations and in continuation to the above referred intimations we wish to inform you that on 27th November 2
findings.why_it_matters: A rating action is a third party revising its view. Downgrades frequently cluster before a payment failure, and the commentary usually names the concern.
findings.investigate: Open the attachment and record what specifically was said, by whom, and whether the issuer's next filing addressed it.

findings.what_changed: The 45-day SEBI LODR deadline for standalone results for the period ending 2019-12-31 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 58 days.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-02-14 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: The most recent parseable results filing was disseminated 2025-02-14, 606 days ago.
findings.why_it_matters: An issuer that has stopped filing cannot be assessed. For a delisted or suspended issuer this is expected; for an active one it is itself the finding.
findings.investigate: Confirm whether the issuer is still listed and still required to file.
findings.counterevidence: Delisting, suspension, merger or voluntary wind-down all stop the filing stream legitimately.

findings.what_changed: The 45-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2018-06-30 passed with no filing. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2018-08-14 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: The 45-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2018-09-30 passed with no filing. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2018-11-14 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.

findings.what_changed: 3 of 27 quarters between 2018-06-30 and 2024-12-31 have no machine-readable filing: 2019-03-31, 2019-06-30, 2019-09-30.
findings.why_it_matters: A gap is not evidence of a problem, but it bounds what can be claimed. Any trend drawn across a gap is an assumption.
findings.investigate: NSE published results XBRL only from about 2019. For earlier periods use the results PDF attached to the announcement stream.

findings.what_changed: The 77-day SEBI LODR deadline for results for the period ending 2020-06-30 passed with no filing. The issuer's trailing median lag was 58 days. The same figure was filed on both the standalone and consolidated basis.
findings.why_it_matters: A missed results deadline is one of the few distress signals that does not depend on the reported figures being accurate. It usually means the accounts are contested, the auditor has not signed, or a valuation is unresolved.
findings.investigate: Check the exchange announcements from 2020-09-15 onward for an intimation of delay, an auditor communication, or a board-meeting postponement.
findings.counterevidence: A late filing is not always issuer-specific: SEBI's COVID-19 relaxations are already applied to the two periods they covered. Check whether any other market-wide extension was in force.
